artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: per-file layer table, fail-loud layer_of, restored 7-line allowlist, assertion C, six observed negative tests, document updates, acceptance criteria by command.

completion_data.completion_summary: Layered the three language directories per file (30-row origin-keyed table) in scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py, made layer_of raise for any unmatched module under FormalSystem/, restored the upward allowlist in scripts/check-metalogic-cycles.sh to the 7 measured MinusLanguage/AxiomDischarge -> Theorems lines, and added a named syntax-before-semantics assertion. All six failure directions were negative-tested by hand on the real tree, and ORGANISATION.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and six further documents now state the measured order with the blind-spot note removed.

memory_candidates.content: When a layer/ownership lookup returns None for unmatched paths, a file move into an uncovered directory silently removes its edges from every measurement built on the lookup, and an equality-asserted allowlist then 'passes' on an empty set. Make the lookup raise for anything inside the library root that matches no row (return None only for genuinely external modules), add a stale-row report for the reverse drift, and add a non-vacuity guard to any assertion whose sets are derived from a table. A shortfall against an allowlist has two causes - the import was removed, or it stopped being measured - and the remediation hint should say so.

In this repo, editing a module docstring in any FormalSystem .lean file changes line counts recorded in generated inventory blocks (README.md 'Live comment lines', FormalSystem/README.md per-file rows); check-module-invariants.sh INV goes red until `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory` is run and the two READMEs are committed.

Hand negative tests on real files in a shared working tree: run each as ONE shell invocation that saves the file with `cp -p` to a scratch dir (mtime preserved, so lake does not rebuild), edits, runs the gate capturing output and exit code, restores unconditionally, then confirms with `git diff --quiet -- <path>`. Never use git checkout/restore to revert (blocked by the destructive-git guard on a dirty tree); remove scratch files with rm.
